enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1052 AM MDT Sat Oct 31 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1100 AM MDT Sat Oct 31 2026

 - Cloudy, mild weather for Halloween. Spotty rain showers west,
   but mostly dry tonight. 

 - Pacific cold front will bring scattered showers and
   thunderstorms on Sunday. Storms will be capable of heavy rain
   and flooding across Southwest New Mexico, in particular the
   Gila Wilderness. A Flood Watch is in effect for portions of
   Grant and Hidalgo Counties.

 - A much-needed stretch of quieter weather is expected next week
   with dry conditions and typical early November temperatures.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 AM MDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Quite a bit of mid-and-high-level cloud coverage for our 
Halloween this year with plenty of moisture aloft. Precipitable 
water values should still be in the 1.0-1.2" range, well above 
normal for the end of October. Broad ridging flow aloft and the 
lack of surface instability due to cloud coverage will lead to a 
"mostly" dry forecast for Halloween night. Can't rule out a stray 
rain shower or two across Southwest New Mexico, but 95% of the 
region will be dry tonight. Temperatures will peak in the upper 
60s/lower 70s this afternoon, only cooling a few degrees tonight 
with the aforementioned clouds keeping us rather mild overnight.
Wind will be light and variable. I don't see anything that will 
interrupt outdoor festivities tonight, so have fun everybody!

Two features to focus on for Sunday fixed across the Southwestern
U.S. will be a strengthening subtropical jet streak reaching 
95-knots at 500mb and a diving Pacific low right behind it. This 
will lead to yet another round of rain chances for the area, along
with a frontal boundary passage between the Sunday evening-early 
Monday morning timeframe. Scattered rain showers beginning along 
the AZ/NM state line as early as Sunday morning will bring a risk 
of training storms and flash flooding through the day. Main risk 
will be across Grant/Hidalgo Counties Sunday afternoon in time 
with frontal passage. Enhanced lifting along the front will lead 
to more widespread showers and thunderstorms, with a storm motion 
parallel to the boundary due to the subtropical jet aloft posing a
risk of training storms and heavy rain "streaks". Most likely
rainfall across Grant County will be 0.50-1.00, but a few spots 
of 1.50-2.00" will be possible. A Flood Watch is in effect for 
most of the Gila and upper Mimbres watersheds. Breezy southwest 
winds will exist ahead of this Pacific front, generally 20-30 mph 
Sunday afternoon across Southwest New Mexico.

Less concerned about heavy rain for the Rio Grande valley and
south-central New Mexico region as dry air entrainment at the 
base of the Pacific low may lead to weaker and lower coverage rain
showers. Even less concerned further SE into Far West Texas, 
where rain chances are lower. Still, we can expect scattered rain 
showers Sunday night-Monday morning for the I-25/US-54 corridors 
as the frontal boundary moves through.

Full-on dry-slotting on Monday behind the Pacific low. This will 
lead to a breezy and cool dry with mostly clear skies. West winds 
15 to 20 mph is the current forecast. A few lingering rain showers
may exist over the Sacramento Mountains, but are not expected to
last through Monday morning.

Dare I say it, next week finally looks dry for New Mexico and 
west Texas. This will be a much-needed reprieve from rain after a
very wet September and October. Lowland highs in the lower 70s 
will be right near normal for early November. No major swings in 
temperature expected and winds look generally light.

&&

(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1100 AM MDT Sat Oct 31 2026

VMC through forecast period with skies SCT-BKN120, BKN250. FEW020
over mtns at KELP next few hours. Surface winds 140-180 AOB 5 
knots this afternoon, becoming light and variable overnight. 
Isolated -RA across SW NM this evening, which may affect KDMN. 
Left out of TAF due to low confidence and minimal impacts.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1100 AM MDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Light and variable winds overnight with continued cloud cover for
your Halloween. Overnight temperatures will stay warm due to cloud
coverage.

Pacific storm system will approach the area on Sunday, with 
breezy southwest winds winds ahead of it. Sustained speeds 20 to 
30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph Sunday afternoon will lead to Good 
vent rates. Scattered showers and thunderstorms beginning Sunday
morning across Gila NF will spread eastward across Southern New
Mexico and Lincoln NF Sunday night into Monday morning. Localized
heavy rain will lead to a flood risk for Gila NF Sunday 
afternoon.

Conditions becoming dry again on Monday, with a week of dry
weather and light winds ahead. Vent rates generally look Poor to
Fair each afternoon going forward. Few day-to-day changes in 
temperature next week, typical for early November. Fire danger
will remain low due to seasonally high ERCs.
